title: session-sandwich-econ-needle-scan
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft that explores a small family of sessionized workloads we call the 'session sandwich' pattern: many short prompting turns punctuated by occasional long context retrievals. Goal is to show relative latency and unit-cost tradeoffs for a handful of realistic serving configurations (batching strategies, KV-cache settings, quantization) and to produce simple text-first charts that help product and infra teams decide default knobs for Optimize recommendations.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR)
- For session-sandwich workloads: small-window prefix caching + opportunistic multiplexing delivers the most consistent p90 improvement while containing cost drift.
- Aggressive static batching increases throughput but hurts p99 for the infrequent long-turns; recommend dynamic small-batch + preempt path.
- Int8 quantization reduces GPU token cost by ~25–35% with modest p90 regressions on long-turns; combine with prefetch to preserve latency.

Methodology
- Workload mix (derived from internal traces, anonymized):
  - 70% short-turns (prompt tokens 8–32, completion tokens 12–40)
  - 25% medium-turns (prompt tokens 64–128, completion 32–80)
  - 5% long-retrieval turns (prompt tokens 512–2048, completion 64–200)
- Target model: open-llm-13B variants (fp16 baseline, int8 quantized).
- Hardware: H100 (80GB), A100 (80GB) as primary comparison points.
- Measured: p50, p90, p99 latency per turn; token-level GPU cost estimate (dollars per 1k output tokens extrapolated from infra cost model).
- Each scenario ran 10k synthetic sessionized conversations (30–120 turns each) to capture KV-cache hit patterns and slot contention.

Configs evaluated
1) On-demand (no batching, no caching) — baseline
2) Small-window prefix caching (store last 8 prompts per session) + opportunistic batch window 10ms
3) Static medium batched (batch size 32) with warm KV prefetch for long turns
4) Dynamic multiplex (multiplex slots to keep GPU utilization high) + int8 quantization
5) Hybrid: small-window cache + dynamic multiplex + int8 (recommended candidate)

Representative text charts (ASCII tables and sparklines)
Table: p90 and p99 latencies (ms) by config on H100 (median over runs)\
| config                                | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | cost($/1k tokens) |
|---------------------------------------|---------|---------|-------------------|
| 1) On-demand                          | 210     | 820     | 1.00              |
| 2) Small-window cache + 10ms window   | 150     | 520     | 0.87              |
| 3) Static batch 32 + prefetch         | 135     | 980     | 0.72              |
| 4) Dynamic multiplex + int8           | 180     | 610     | 0.62              |
| 5) Hybrid (cache + multiplex + int8)  | 140     | 560     | 0.58              |

Simple latency distribution sketch (p50/p90/p99 bars, longer = worse)
On-demand        : p50[==] p90[=====] p99[===================]
Cache+10ms       : p50[==] p90[===]  p99[=============]
Static-batch-32  : p50[===]p90[==]   p99[========================]
Dynamic+int8     : p50[==] p90[====]  p99[==============]
Hybrid           : p50[===]p90[===]  p99[=============]

Interpretation notes
- Static batching (config 3) gives the lowest average p90 in this mix because it amortizes token compute very well for medium turns; however, long-turn p99 suffers because batch formation + memory pressure delays servicing an outlier long request. The p99 inflation is visible and could violate strict SLOs.
- Caching (config 2) provides the best p90 improvement for short-turn dominated mixes, with modest cost savings from reduced attention compute (prefix removal). It does little for the long retrieval turns unless paired with prefetch.
- Int8 quantization (config 4) yields strong cost reduction but makes long-turn variance slightly worse due to heavier kernel fragmentation; pairing with dynamic multiplex mitigates the p99 hit.
- The Hybrid config (5) balances cost and tail latency well in this workload: cache reduces most short-turn work, multiplexing keeps GPUs busy without large batches, and int8 brings down unit cost.

Cost sensitivity sweep (text table across hardware)
Assumes baseline $/token (fp16 on H100) = 1.0 (relative)
- H100 fp16 baseline: 1.00
- H100 int8 (same config): 0.68–0.72 (observed 0.70)
- A100 fp16 (same config): 1.12 (slightly higher runtime cost due to kernel efficiency)
- A100 int8: 0.80–0.86
Takeaway: H100 + int8 is best for pure unit economics, but A100 still acceptable if H100 not available; tail-latency differences can flip choice depending on SLO priority.

Microbench sparks (tiny ascii sparkline of p99 by config)
On-demand : ▁▂▃▄▇▇▇▇▇ (big tail)
Cache+10ms: ▁▁▂▂▇▇▇ (reduced long tail)
Static32   : ▁▁▁▇▇▇▇▇▇ (tight p90 but large p99 spike)
Dynamic+int8: ▁▂▂▃▆▇▇ (moderate tail)
Hybrid      : ▁▁▂▂▅▆▇ (best balanced)

Operational considerations and unanswered questions
- Cold start penalty distribution for long-turn sessions: our synthetic runs pre-warm ~20% of sessions. Need to run an explicit cold-start sweep (session-level prewarm=0) to quantify worst-case p99 for Private deployments.
- Memory fragmentation under int8 paths: observed intermittent host->device stalls in A100 runs; recommend deeper microprofiling (CUDA NVTX traces) for quantized kernels.
- Multitenancy effects: these runs were single-tenant; slot contention under real multi-tenant traffic likely amplifies p99 for static batching. We should re-run with 3 tenant profiles.

Recommendations (short)
- Default recommendation for Optimize for session-sandwich workloads: Hybrid (small-window prefix cache + dynamic multiplex + int8) behind a canary rollout. Rationale: best combined p90/p99 containment with >20% cost reduction vs baseline.
- For strict p99 SLO customers: prefer small-window cache + conservative multiplexing (avoid static large batches) and optionally fp16 on H100.
- Add a focused benchmark job to nightly CI to capture cold-start tails and multi-tenant contention.

Action items (who/when)
- Product-optimize: draft configuration knobs and cost/latency slider for console. Owner: Clara Nguyen. Due: 2028-07-09.
- Infra/perf: NVTX traces and int8 microprofile on A100. Owner: Ravi Patel. Due: 2028-07-06.
- SRE: multi-tenant simulated run (3 tenants) and multi-region variation. Owner: Lena Ortiz. Due: 2028-07-12.

Appendix: short-run raw numbers (sampled averages from one representative run, H100)
- Config 1 (On-demand): p50 120ms, p90 210ms, p99 820ms, cost 1.00
- Config 2 (Cache+10ms): p50 95ms, p90 150ms, p99 520ms, cost 0.87
- Config 3 (Static batch32): p50 85ms, p90 135ms, p99 980ms, cost 0.72
- Config 4 (Dynamic+int8): p50 110ms, p90 180ms, p99 610ms, cost 0.62
- Config 5 (Hybrid): p50 88ms, p90 140ms, p99 560ms, cost 0.58

Notes on reproducibility
- Benchmark code and notebook: gs://benchmarks/session-sandwich-jun28-2028.ipynb (linked). Use the run_bench.sh wrapper which sets seeds and synthetic session sampler.
- Hardware labels: H100 = cloud-h100-80g-prod, A100 = cloud-a100-80g-prod. Make sure driver 535.x is used for int8 kernels.

This doc is a working draft — gaps are called out above. Feedback welcome directly in the doc or in the linked JIRA OPT-1287.
